E01-byd-company-limited: BYD Company Limited, also known as Blade Battery, is a Chinese multinational company specializing in cells and chemistry. As a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader, the company operates primarily in the manufacture of lithium-ion batteries for various applications. Based in China, BYD Company Limited has established itself as a significant player in the global battery industry.
E01-lg-energy-solution: LG Energy Solution is a South Korean company that operates in the cells and chemistry sector as a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader. The company specializes in producing NMC pouch and cylindrical cells for global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs). Founded in 2020, LG Energy Solution is listed on the Korea Stock Exchange under the ticker KRX: 373220 and primarily produces NMC and LFP chemistry-based cells in a 46-series form factor. The company supplies cells to General Motors as part of its relationship with the automaker's Ultium Platform project, which also involves a joint venture between the two companies.
E01-panasonic: Panasonic is a Japanese multinational corporation that manufactures cells and chemistry products. As a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the sector of Cells & Chemistry, Panasonic produces cylindrical cells, including the 2170 and 4680 formats. The company supplies battery cells to Tesla's Battery Division, with its products used in various applications.
E01-samsung-sdi: Samsung SDI is a South Korean company that manufactures cells and provides battery solutions. The company specializes in producing prismatic and cylindrical lithium-nickel-manganese-cobalt-oxide (NMC) batteries, which are used in various applications including electric vehicles. As part of its supply chain, Samsung SDI supplies batteries to the Volkswagen Group's PowerCo division.
E01-sk-on: SK On is a South Korean company that manufactures pouch cells, primarily in the form of Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) chemistry. As part of its Loop stage, SK On focuses on manufacturing. The company operates under the Ford BlueOval SK Joint Venture with Ford's EV Division, supplying them with pouch-cell products.
E01-tesla: Tesla's Battery Division is a leading manufacturer of lithium-ion cells and energy storage systems. Based in the USA, the company operates under the sector of Cells & Chemistry as one of Major Cell Manufacturers & Gigafactory Leaders. Founded in 2003, Tesla is an active public corporation that has pioneered the electric vehicle (EV) industry with its in-house cell technology, including the 4680 cylindrical cell and Megapack ESS. The company's chemistry primarily involves Nickel-Cobalt-Aluminum (NCA) and Lithium-Ferrophosphate (LFP).
E01-northvolt: Northvolt is a Swedish company that manufactures lithium-ion cells and operates as a major cell manufacturer in the sector. The firm was founded in 2016 by Peter Carlsson, an ex-Tesla executive, with a focus on recycling and closed-loop production. Northvolt's products are primarily based on Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) chemistry and come in both prismatic and cylindrical form factors.
E01-eve-energy-co-ltd: EVE Energy Co., Ltd. is a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the Cells & Chemistry sector. Based in China, the company specializes in the manufacture of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, with a focus on large-format cylindrical designs. EVE Energy's products are categorized as 46-series cylindrical cells, which fall under the prismatic and cylindrical form factor categories. The company operates as a publicly traded entity.
E01-gotion-high-tech: Gotion High-tech, also known as Guoxuan High-tech, is a Chinese company that specializes in the manufacture of lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) cells. As a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the sector, it plays a significant role in the global energy storage industry. The company supplies its products to Volkswagen Group's PowerCo division, with Volkswagen being one of its major shareholders.
E01-quantumscape: QuantumScape is a solid-state battery manufacturer based in the USA. The company develops ceramic separators and anode-free solid-state batteries, backed by Volkswagen Group. As a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader, QuantumScape operates under the Loop stage of manufacture. Its shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) under ticker symbol QS.
E02-nio: NIO is a Chinese premium electric vehicle (EV) manufacturer that specializes in the development and deployment of battery swapping technology, known as Power Swap. The company was founded to pioneer the use of battery swapping in electric vehicles, aiming to provide faster and more convenient charging experiences for customers. NIO's products are designed to be environmentally friendly and technologically advanced, with a focus on software integration and data analytics. As a publicly traded company, NIO operates in China and leverages software solutions from Voltaiq, a leading provider of battery intelligence platforms.
E02-ford: Ford's Electric Vehicle Division is a subsidiary of the American multinational automaker Ford Motor Company. The division is part of Ford's broader strategy to expand its electric vehicle offerings and capabilities, with a focus on deploying and utilizing electric vehicles and charging infrastructure. Based in the United States, Ford's EV Division operates under the brand name BlueOval SK, in partnership with South Korean battery manufacturer SK On, and also oversees the development of BlueOval City, a planned automotive manufacturing facility.
E02-general-motors: General Motors is a leading American automaker that focuses on the development and deployment of electric vehicles, energy storage systems, and charging infrastructure. The company's Ultium Platform is a comprehensive battery system designed for various applications, including EVs and ESS. As part of its efforts to expand its presence in the emerging EV market, General Motors has established an automotive battery joint venture with LG Energy Solution (LGES) called Ultium Cells.
E02-volkswagen-group: Volkswagen Group is a German multinational automotive manufacturing corporation. As part of its efforts to expand into electric vehicles, the company has established PowerCo, a cell unit focused on solid-state batteries. Additionally, Volkswagen Group has made investments in QuantumScape and Gotion High-tech, further solidifying its presence in the electric vehicle sector.
E02-xiaomi: Xiaomi is a Chinese multinational company that specializes in consumer electronics and automotive products. As a leading player in the electric vehicle (EV) market, Xiaomi has established itself as a significant force in the Automotive OEMs - EV Focus category. The company's origins date back to 2010 when it was founded by Lei Jun, and since then, it has grown into one of the world's largest consumer electronics companies. With its public ownership structure, Xiaomi continues to operate actively in the market.
E03-umicore: Umicore is a Belgian company that specializes in cathode materials and battery recycling. Founded in 1989, the company has established itself as a leading provider of NMC cathode materials and a pioneer in closed-loop recycling. Umicore supplies its products to major customers such as Samsung SDI and is also a member of the Global Battery Alliance, further solidifying its position within the industry.
E03-basf: BASF is a German-based company operating in the Materials & Components sector. The company supplies cathode active materials and battery chemicals as part of its Battery Materials & Performance Plastics division. As a leading chemical manufacturer, BASF's products are used in various applications, including batteries. Its shares are listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol ETR: BAS.
E03-posco-future-m: POSCO Future M is a South Korean company that operates as the cathode and anode materials arm of POSCO Chemical. The company falls under the Materials & Components sector, specifically within the Cell Materials category. As a public entity, POSCO Future M is actively engaged in refining its products, which include active materials for cathodes and anodes, electrolytes, and separators.
E03-ecopro-bm: EcoPro BM is a South Korean company specializing in the production of high-nickel cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries. As a leading supplier of NCA/NMC cathodes, the company's products are used in various applications, including electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. EcoPro BM is listed on the public stock market and operates as an active corporate entity. The company supplies its cathode materials to Samsung SDI, a prominent battery manufacturer.
E03-novonix-limited: Novonix Limited is a publicly traded company based in Australia that specializes in the production of synthetic graphite anodes for battery applications. The company's products are used in various industries, including energy storage and electric vehicles. Novonix Limited has established a supply relationship with LG Energy Solution, one of the leading players in the global battery market. As a materials and components supplier, the company's primary focus is on refining its synthetic graphite anode product for use in battery testing equipment.
E03-sila-nanotechnologies: Sila Nanotechnologies is a private materials and components company that specializes in silicon anode materials. Founded by Gene Berdichevsky, a former Tesla engineer, the company was established in 2011. Sila Nanotechnologies' primary product is its silicon anode material, which it targets at electric vehicle cell makers and consumer electronics companies. The company supplies its products to Panasonic Energy, among other clients.
E03-group14-technologies: Group14 Technologies is a private materials and components company specializing in silicon-carbon anodes. The company's product, SCC55, is a silicon-carbon anode material used in various applications. Group14 Technologies has partnered with SK and Porsche to further develop its technology, while also collaborating with SK On as part of its joint venture.
E04-analog-devices-inc: Analog Devices, Inc. is a publicly traded company listed on the NASDAQ under ticker symbol ADI. The company operates in the power electronics and battery management system (BMS) sectors. Analog Devices manufactures BMS ICs, including wireless BMS solutions, which were previously part of Maxim Integrated's business. The company supplies General Motors with its BMS technology as part of the Ultium Platform.
E04-infineon-technologies: Infineon Technologies is a leading manufacturer of power electronics and battery management systems (BMS). The company's product portfolio includes silicon carbide (SiC) solutions for electric vehicle (EV) inverters. As a publicly traded entity, Infineon Technologies operates as a corporate entity with an active presence in the industry.
E04-wolfspeed: Wolfspeed is a publicly traded company that specializes in the manufacture of silicon-carbide (SiC) products for power electronics and battery management systems. As a pure-play player in the EV power electronics sector, Wolfspeed supplies critical components to major automotive manufacturers. The company's products are used in various applications, including electric vehicles, where they enable more efficient and reliable power delivery.
E05-li-cycle: Li-Cycle is a publicly traded company that operates as a spoke-and-hub lithium-ion recycler. The company produces black mass and battery-grade metals, including Li, Ni, and Co. As an active corporate entity, Li-Cycle supplies its products to Glencore's recycling operations.
E05-redwood-materials: Redwood Materials is a private company based in the USA that operates as a closed-loop recycler and cathode/anode-foil manufacturer. The firm was founded in 2017 by JB Straubel, former Tesla CTO, and specializes in recovering and processing recycled materials for use in battery production. Redwood Materials supplies cathode and copper foil to Panasonic Energy and also provides recycling services for Ford's electric vehicle division. The company competes with Albemarle Corporation, a leading lithium producer.
E05-ascend-elements: Ascend Elements, formerly known as Battery Resourcers, is a private company operating in the recycling and circular economy sector. The firm specializes in hydro-to-cathode direct recycling of lithium-ion batteries to produce pCAM/CAM, a key material for electric vehicle batteries. As an active corporate entity, Ascend Elements supplies LG Energy Solution with its recycled materials.
E05-cirba-solutions: Cirba Solutions is a private company that operates in the recycling and circular economy sector, specializing in the recovery of battery materials. The company was previously known as Retriev Technologies before rebranding under its current name. Cirba Solutions has developed a scrap-trading platform called Radix, which facilitates the exchange of recyclable materials. As part of its operations, the company recycles materials for General Motors, supporting the production of the Ultium Platform.
E05-brunp-recycling: Brunp Recycling is the recycling subsidiary of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL). As a closed-loop cathode metals recovery operation, Brunp Recycling focuses on recovering and reusing valuable materials. The company operates within the sector of Recycling & Circular Economy, specifically in the category of Recycling & Second Life.
E05-glencore: Glencore is a Swiss-based company that operates in the recycling and circular economy sector. As a diversified miner and trader, it recovers valuable metals such as cobalt, nickel, and copper from various sources. The company's primary focus is on Li-ion recycling, with its products being supplied to Umicore for use in cathode materials.
E05-ganfeng-lithium: Ganfeng Lithium's Recycling Division is a segment of the company that focuses on recovering lithium from various sources. The division operates in China and recovers lithium compounds and metal through extraction methods including brine, hard rock, and recycling. As a vertically integrated company, Ganfeng Lithium produces lithium compounds and metal for use in battery production, with its products supplied to major customers such as Tesla's Battery Division and LG Energy Solution.
E06-argonne-national-laboratory: Argonne National Laboratory is a research institute operated by the United States Department of Energy. The CAMP (Cellular Materials Processing) facility at Argonne is a cell-fabrication and battery production hub, while the Battery500 and ReCell facilities serve as standards and media for the energy storage industry. As a national laboratory, Argonne conducts research in various fields, including energy storage, materials science, and nanotechnology. The lab is funded by the US Department of Energy.
E06-national-renewable-energy-laboratory: The National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) is a research institute and national laboratory located in Golden, Colorado. As part of the United States Department of Energy's (DOE) renewable energy program, NREL conducts research and development in various areas related to renewable energy technologies. The laboratory provides testing and analysis services for battery systems, among other applications.
E07-bloombergnef: BloombergNEF is a media organization that provides clean-energy research and data on batteries, storage, and electric vehicles. The company operates under the category of Industry News, Analysis & Regional Portals within the Research, Standards & Media sector. As an active entity, BloombergNEF offers research and data services to its audience. It has a specific relationship with Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL), a leading battery manufacturer.
E07-benchmark-mineral-intelligence: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence is a research and standards organization that provides price-reporting services for the battery supply chain. The company operates as a data house, offering insights and analysis to support informed decision-making in the industry. Benchmark Mineral Intelligence focuses on lithium, a key component in battery production, and has established relationships with major players such as Albemarle Corporation. By covering market trends and prices, the organization aims to facilitate transparency and understanding within the battery supply chain.
E08-global-battery-alliance: The Global Battery Alliance is a research, standards, and media association that hosts the World Economic Forum (WEF). It is an industry alliance focused on advancing battery technology. The GBA is behind the development of the Battery Passport standard, which aims to improve the sustainability of the global battery ecosystem. As an active institution, it continues to work towards its goals in the field of research and standards.
E10-voltaiq: Voltaiq is a private software company that provides an enterprise battery-intelligence platform, designed to support manufacturers and original equipment manufacturers. The platform offers data-driven insights to optimize battery performance and longevity. Voltaiq's solution is deployed as a Software as a Service (SaaS) offering in the cloud. As a corporate entity, it operates under the category of Data, Software, AI & Cloud within the Enablers loop stage.
E10-twaice: Twaice is a private company that provides battery analytics software for various industries. Founded in 2018, the company offers its software as a service (SaaS) on a cloud-based platform. Its product is designed to support electric vehicle fleets, grid energy storage systems (ESS), and research and development activities in cell manufacturing.
E10-accure-battery-intelligence: Accure Battery Intelligence is a private software company that provides cloud-based battery analytics solutions for electric vehicle (EV) and energy storage system (ESS) fleets. The company's platform offers real-time insights into the safety and performance of these batteries, enabling fleet operators to optimize their operations and extend the lifespan of their assets. As an Enabler in the Data, Software, AI & Cloud category, Accure Battery Intelligence is part of a growing ecosystem that supports the development and deployment of sustainable energy solutions.
E11-albemarle-corporation: Albemarle Corporation is the world's largest lithium producer, extracting lithium carbonate and hydroxide from both hard-rock sources at its Greenbushes mine in Australia and brine deposits in Chile's Atacama region. The company also produces bromine as a byproduct of its operations. As a publicly traded entity, Albemarle Corporation is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol ALB. It has been a member of the Global Battery Alliance since its inception and supplies lithium to major battery manufacturers such as Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (CATL) and LG Energy Solution.
E11-sqm: SQM is a Chilean mining company that extracts lithium and specialty chemicals from the Atacama salar. The company operates in the raw materials and mining sector, with its primary product being lithium carbonate and hydroxide. As a publicly traded entity listed on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker NYSE: SQM, SQM is an active player in the global market for lithium and other specialty chemicals.
E11-arcadium-lithium-plc: Arcadium Lithium plc is a publicly traded mining company formed in 2024 through the merger of Livent and Allkem. The company operates as an extract stage entity, primarily producing lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate. Following its acquisition by Rio Tinto in 2025, Arcadium Lithium continues to be active in the industry, with its shares listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol NYSE: ALTM.
E11-pilbara-minerals: Pilbara Minerals is an Australian mining company that produces spodumene concentrate from hard-rock deposits. The company operates the Pilgangoora mine in Western Australia, which is its primary source of production. As a publicly traded entity, Pilbara Minerals supplies spodumene concentrate to various customers, including Ganfeng Lithium's Recycling Division.
E11-bhp: BHP Nickel is a subsidiary of BHP Group, a global resources company. The company operates the Nickel West mine in Western Australia, which produces nickel for use in battery cathodes. As part of its supply agreement with Tesla's Battery Division, BHP Nickel supplies materials to support the production of lithium-ion batteries at Gigafactory 1 in Nevada.
E11-vale-s-a: Vale S.A. is a Brazilian mining company that operates in the raw materials and mining sector, with its primary product being nickel. As one of the world's largest nickel producers, Vale extracts and processes nickel ore to supply various industries. The company is headquartered in Brazil and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol VALE, making it a publicly traded entity.
E11-syrah-resources: Syrah Resources is a publicly traded mining company that operates in the raw materials sector. The company's primary business involves extracting and processing natural and active anode graphite, with operations primarily located in Australia. Syrah Resources also has a significant presence in Mozambique, where it mines graphite at its Balama deposit.
E12-wuxi-lead-intelligent-equipment: Wuxi Lead Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd. is a public company that operates in the manufacturing equipment and factory sector, specifically within the category of equipment and front-end manufacturing. The company specializes in designing and manufacturing turnkey battery-manufacturing lines, positioning itself as the world's largest supplier in this field. As a leading manufacturer, Wuxi Lead Intelligent Equipment Co., Ltd. supplies its products to prominent companies such as CATL, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited.
E12-manz-ag: Manz AG is a German-based company that specializes in the manufacture of high-precision assembly and stacking equipment. As a leading supplier in its sector, Manz AG provides products for various industries, including those involved in battery production. The company's products are used globally, with notable partnerships established with companies such as Northvolt. Manz AG is listed on the stock exchange and operates as an active entity within the public sector.
E13-fluence: Fluence is a publicly traded company listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol FLNC. The company operates as a grid-scale Energy Storage Systems (ESS) integrator, leveraging its origins as a joint venture between Siemens and AES. Fluence provides ESS solutions to customers in the United States, utilizing software from Accure Battery Intelligence for its operations.
E13-sungrow-power-supply-co: Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. is a leading manufacturer of photovoltaic inverters and energy storage systems (ESS) based in China. As a prominent player in the sector, the company offers products that cater to the growing demand for renewable energy solutions. Sungrow's products are deployed and used globally, with a focus on supporting the transition to sustainable energy sources.
E13-byd: BYD (ESS) is a Chinese company that specializes in the production of electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in 1995, BYD has established itself as a leading manufacturer of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, known for their efficiency and reliability. The company's products include LFP Blade cells used in electric vehicles and other applications, with exports primarily routed through the Port of Rotterdam.
E14-breakthrough-energy-ventures: Breakthrough Energy Ventures is a private investment firm focused on supporting the development of battery and materials technologies. The company was established by Bill Gates as part of his climate fund initiative, with the goal of backing innovative startups working on sustainable energy solutions. As an Enabler in the Loop stage, Breakthrough Energy Ventures has invested in several companies, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and Sila Nanotechnologies, to support their research and development efforts.
E18-trumpf-gmbh-co-kg: Trumpf GmbH + Co. KG is a German private company that specializes in manufacturing equipment, particularly in the thermal, welding, and finishing sector. As a leading manufacturer of laser technology, the company primarily focuses on welding and cutting solutions for cell and pack assembly. Trumpf supplies its products to various industries, including automotive and electronics, and has established partnerships with other companies such as Northvolt.
E19-dhl: DHL is a global logistics company that provides a range of services including dangerous goods and battery supply chain solutions. As part of its Logistics & Supply Chain category, DHL operates in various geography locations around the world. The company's services link different stages of the supply chain, from customs clearance to delivery.
E19-kuehne-nagel: Kuehne + Nagel is a global logistics company that provides freight forwarding services, including battery and hazmat transportation, as well as customs clearance. The company operates in various locations around the world, offering its services to clients across multiple industries. As a publicly traded entity, Kuehne + Nagel is subject to regulatory oversight and market fluctuations.
E19-port-of-rotterdam: The Port of Rotterdam is Europe's largest port, serving as a primary hub for the import and export of goods. It is particularly notable for its role in handling Asian cell imports and European electric vehicle (EV) exports. As a deep-water port and container terminal facility, it has a capacity to handle approximately 15 million Twenty-Foot Equivalent Units (TEU). Located in Rotterdam, the port plays a crucial strategic role as the primary EU import hub for Asian cells.
E22-chargepoint: ChargePoint is a leading provider of electric vehicle charging solutions in North America. As a publicly traded company, it operates one of the largest public charging networks in the region, offering a range of services including Level 2 and DC Fast Charging stations. With a strong presence across the United States and Canada, ChargePoint provides charging infrastructure to various industries, including fleet operators, retailers, and residential customers. The company's network spans over 40,000 charging points, making it a prominent player in the electric vehicle charging market.
E25-the-faraday-institution: The Faraday Institution is a UK-based research consortium established by the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) to support battery research. As the UK's flagship battery research programme, it aims to develop a talent pipeline for the sector. The institution focuses on advancing battery technology through collaborative research initiatives. Its work contributes to the development of sustainable energy solutions.
E26-prof-jeff-dahn: Prof. Jeff Dahn is a professor at Dalhousie University and the academic research partner of Tesla on lithium-ion battery technology. He is recognized as a pioneer in the field of cell longevity and has expertise in electrolytes. As part of his role, Prof. Dahn contributes to events, media, and community activities related to energy and technology.
E26-elon-musk: Elon Musk is the CEO of Tesla, a position he has held since 2008. He is also the founder of SpaceX, a private aerospace manufacturer and space transport services company. As CEO of Tesla's Battery Division and lead on its Gigafactory strategy, Musk played a key role in driving the development of the 4680 cell technology.
E26-peter-carlsson: Peter Carlsson is a co-founder of Northvolt. He was previously the head of supply chain for Tesla's Battery Division and oversaw operations at one of its Gigafactories. As part of his role, he led efforts to optimize the company's battery supply chain.
E26-jb-straubel: JB Straubel is a founder and CEO of Redwood Materials. He previously worked in the Battery Division of Tesla, where he was involved with the development of Tesla's first pack. Straubel has now shifted his focus to closing the loop at Redwood Materials, which he founded, by architecting sustainable materials solutions for the industry.
E26-gene-berdichevsky: Gene Berdichevsky is a co-founder and CEO of Sila Nanotechnologies, a company he founded to develop silicon-anode batteries. Prior to founding Sila, Berdichevsky was an employee at Tesla's Battery Division, working at one of the company's Gigafactories. As part of his work at Tesla, Berdichevsky held the position of employee #7.
E26-dr-m-stanley-whittingham: Dr. M. Stanley Whittingham is a Nobel laureate and professor at Binghamton University. He invented the lithium intercalation cathode, a significant advancement in battery technology. As an expert in intercalation chemistry, Dr. Whittingham continues to contribute to the field through his research and academic pursuits.
E01-catl: CATL is the world's largest EV and ESS battery maker, operating as a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the Cells & Chemistry sector. Founded in 2011, the company is headquartered in China and listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange under the ticker SZSE: 300750. CATL produces a range of lithium-ion cells, including LFP, NMC, M3P, and Na-ion chemistries, in both prismatic and pouch form factors, with mass production capabilities at its gigafactories. The company supplies batteries to major clients such as Tesla's Battery Division and Volkswagen Group's PowerCo, and also exports through the Port of Rotterdam, while being a member of the Global Battery Alliance.
E01-farasis-energy: Farasis Energy is a Chinese company that operates in the sector of cells and chemistry, specifically as a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader. The company's primary business involves the manufacture of lithium-ion battery cells. Based in China, Farasis Energy is engaged in the production of loop-stage products.
E01-svolt-energy-technology: SVOLT Energy Technology is a leading manufacturer of cells and chemistry products in the industry. Based in China, the company operates as part of the sector of Cells & Chemistry, specifically within the category of Major Cell Manufacturers & Gigafactory Leaders. SVOLT Energy Technology's primary function is to manufacture loop stage products.
E01-aesc: Envision AESC is a leading manufacturer of lithium-ion battery cells and modules. As a major player in the industry, the company has established itself as a key supplier to global automotive and renewable energy markets. With its extensive production capacity, Envision AESC plays a significant role in meeting the growing demand for electric vehicle batteries. The company's manufacturing facilities are strategically located across Asia, enabling efficient supply chain management and logistics.
E01-calb: CALB is a leading manufacturer of lithium batteries, operating primarily in the cells and chemistry sector. Based in China, the company specializes in producing high-quality lithium battery products for various applications. As a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader, CALB has established itself as a significant player in the global lithium battery industry.
E01-sunwoda-electronic: Sunwoda Electronic is a leading manufacturer of cells and a major player in the gigafactory industry. Based in China, the company operates primarily in the loop stage of cell production. As part of its sector, Sunwoda Electronic contributes to the global supply chain for lithium-ion batteries. The company's operations are focused on meeting the growing demand for electric vehicle batteries and other energy storage applications.
E01-china-bak-battery: China BAK Battery is a leading manufacturer of lithium-ion batteries, operating under the category of Major Cell Manufacturers & Gigafactory Leaders in the Cells & Chemistry sector. Based in Shenzhen, China, the company specializes in producing high-quality battery cells for various applications, including electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. With its extensive production capabilities, China BAK Battery plays a significant role in meeting the growing demand for lithium-ion batteries worldwide. The company's products are used by major automotive manufacturers and other industry players globally.
E01-lishen: Tianjin Lishen Battery, also known as Lishen, is a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the cells & chemistry sector. The company is primarily engaged in the manufacture of lithium-ion batteries. With its extensive production capabilities, Lishen has established itself as a significant player in the global battery industry.
E01-microvast: Microvast is a leading manufacturer of cells and chemicals in the United States. As a major player in the industry, it operates under the category of Major Cell Manufacturers & Gigafactory Leaders within Cells & Chemistry. The company's primary focus is on the manufacture loop stage.
E01-prologium-technology: ProLogium Technology is a Taiwanese company specializing in the manufacture of solid-state batteries. As a major player in the cells and chemistry industry, it has established itself as one of the leading gigafactory leaders. The company operates under the category of Major Cell Manufacturers, indicating its significant role in the production of lithium-ion batteries. ProLogium Technology is based in Taiwan and focuses on the development and manufacturing of solid-state battery technology.
E01-solid-power: Solid Power is a leading manufacturer of solid-state batteries in the United States. As part of the Cells & Chemistry sector, the company is recognized for its significant contributions to the development and production of major cell manufacturers and gigafactory leaders. With operations focused on loop stage manufacture, Solid Power plays a crucial role in meeting growing demand for energy storage solutions.
E01-24m-technologies: 24M Technologies is a leading manufacturer of semi-solid materials, operating under the sector of Cells & Chemistry. As a major player in the industry, 24M Technologies has established itself as a significant contributor to the development and production of advanced cell technologies. The company's primary focus is on manufacturing, with its products being utilized in various applications within the cells and chemistry category.
E01-one: ONE (Our Next Energy) is a leading manufacturer of lithium-ion cells and a major player in the gigafactory industry. Based in the United States, the company operates primarily in the sector of Cells & Chemistry. ONE's primary focus is on the manufacture of lithium-ion cells for various applications, including energy storage systems.
E01-freyr-battery: FREYR Battery is a major cell manufacturer based in Norway. The company operates a gigafactory for lithium-ion battery production, primarily serving the electric vehicle and renewable energy sectors. FREYR Battery's products are designed to support the growing demand for sustainable energy solutions.
E01-verkor: Verkor is a French company operating in the sector of cells and chemistry. As a major cell manufacturer, it is recognized for its gigafactory leadership within this category. The company's primary focus is on the manufacture loop stage. Verkor is based in France.
E01-recharge-industries: Recharge Industries is a major cell manufacturer and gigafactory leader in the sector of cells and chemistry. The company, previously known as Britishvolt, operates primarily in the manufacture of lithium-ion batteries for electric vehicles. With its focus on production, Recharge Industries has established itself as a significant player in the industry's loop stage.
E01-acc: The Automotive Cells Company (ACC) is a leading manufacturer of automotive cells, based in France. As a major player in the industry, ACC operates under the category of Major Cell Manufacturers & Gigafactory Leaders within the Cells & Chemistry sector. The company's primary focus is on the manufacture of automotive cells.
E01-inobat-auto: InoBat Auto is a Slovakian company specializing in the manufacture of lithium-ion battery cells. As part of its Loop stage, InoBat Auto focuses on producing high-quality battery cells for various applications, including electric vehicles and renewable energy systems. The company operates in the sector of Cells & Chemistry, which includes major cell manufacturers and gigafactory leaders. Based in Slovakia, InoBat Auto is a significant player in the global battery manufacturing industry.
E01-morrow-batteries: Morrow Batteries is a major cell manufacturer based in Norway. The company operates under the Loop stage, which involves manufacturing cells for various applications.
